summary: The app's primary navigation rail — where you are, and what else there is.

pairs.dont: Mark the current page with the background alone.
pairs.do: Keep the weight change and aria-current that come with `active`.
pairs.why: Hover, focus and selection all tint the row. The weight is what still says which page you are on when the pointer is somewhere else.

pairs.dont: Ship the collapsed rail as the default state.
pairs.do: Default to labels; let people collapse it.
pairs.why: An icon-only rail is a memory test. It is a fine option for someone who already knows the product, and a poor starting point for someone who does not.

pairs.do: Keep to one level, and use a page for anything deeper.
pairs.why: The rail is narrow. Two levels of indent leave no room for the words, and the tree becomes something to navigate rather than navigation.

pairs.dont: Put twelve items in one flat list.
pairs.do: Group them and label the groups.
pairs.why: The labels are what make a long rail scannable — and they are the first thing that disappears when it collapses, which tells you how much work they were doing.

pairs.dont: Use the badge slot for status words.
pairs.do: Keep it to counts of things waiting.
pairs.why: A number in a nav row reads as "this many need you". A word reads as part of the label and makes the row ambiguous.

pairs.dont: Cancel the header's padding with a class so the brand block can bleed.
pairs.why: no-restyle refuses the class, and it should — padding is the header's own decision. The plate bleeds to three edges in both products, so the header offers that shape itself rather than being argued out of its own.

pairs.dont: Hold a new brand's plate back until someone draws its artwork.
pairs.do: Ship it with no image — the plate paints the rail's own surface.
pairs.why: A brand with no asset reads as a quiet header, which is honest. An empty coloured box nobody designed is worse than no plate at all.

pairs.dont: Assume the wordmark reads on whatever image the product supplies.
pairs.do: Look at the asset, and pass ink="on-light" when it is pale.
pairs.why: On a token surface fg/on/* is solved by measurement. Nothing can measure a bitmap, so an image is the one place in the system where contrast is the product's responsibility.

pairs.dont: Dim the second line with opacity.
pairs.do: Let size and weight carry the hierarchy.
pairs.why: There is no on-primary ink below emphasis to reach for, and opacity on text produces a contrast ratio nobody has measured. body/xs under heading/sm separates them without inventing a colour.

a11y: The active item sets aria-current="page" as well as the treatment, so "current" survives when colour does not.
The collapse toggle carries aria-expanded and an aria-label that changes with state — "Expand sidebar" or "Collapse sidebar" — because the icon alone never says which way it goes.
The PanelLeft glyph is aria-hidden; the button's label is its name.
Collapsing changes width with no transition, deliberately: there are no motion tokens yet, so the change is instant rather than arbitrarily timed.
The plate's image is decorative — empty alt and aria-hidden. The wordmark is the accessible text, so a plate whose wordmark is itself artwork needs real text beside it or a label.
Collapsed to 48 the wordmark is replaced by `mark`, so the mark has to still identify the product. A letter does; an abstract glyph on its own does not.
The plate is not a control. If it should navigate home, the product wraps it in a link — it does not become one by sitting at the top.
